sentences.text: Sauropelta was a medium-sized dinosaur with a total length ranging from 5.2 to 6 meters.
Its tail was exceptionally long, making up about half of the animal's entire body size.
Looking down from above, the skull appeared triangular, widening behind the eyes to a maximum width of 35 centimeters before tapering toward the snout.
This heavily built quadruped weighed approximately 1.5 tons and moved on four legs.
Researchers have debated the arrangement of its armor, with early views of a single row replaced by a reconstruction of two parallel rows stacked on each side.
John Ostrom formally named the genus Sauropelta in the year 1970.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as AMNH 3032, was a partial skeleton gathered by Barnum Brown in Big Horn County, Montana, during the early 1930s.
To date, only one species, Sauropelta edwardsorum, is known to exist within this genus.
Living in an era before grasses evolved, this herbivore likely browsed on conifers and cycads using a narrow snout adapted for selective feeding.
Its defense strategy involved falling to the ground and digging its feet in to stop predators from flipping it over.
The bases of the cervical dorsal spines and caudal plates were fused, which significantly limited movement in the neck and the front section of the tail.
It inhabited wide plains near rivers that drained into a shallow inland sea, where forests of conifers covered the landscape.
Since its initial description, Sauropelta has been classified as a member of the family Nodosauridae.
This animal lived during the Early Cretaceous Period, specifically around 108.5 million years ago in the Albian stage, in what is now North America.
A related nodosaurid found in the Poison Strip Sandstone of Utah is considered contemporaneous with these specimens.
Its territory shared space with the small ornithopod Zephyrosaurus, a few titanosaurians, and an unknown ornithomimosaurian.

The Cloverly ecosystem featured a complex food web where the apex predator was the large carcharodontosaurid theropod Acrocanthosaurus, while smaller predators like Deinonychus, Microvenator, and large alosauroids also hunted herbivores.
